declarations.en: Let $K$ be a characteristic-zero field satisfying the curve-field assumption: there is an element $s∈K$ with no nonzero polynomial over $ℚ$ vanishing at $s$, and $K$ is finite dimensional over the subfield $ℚ(s)$ generated by $ℚ$ and $s$. A place $P$ means a valuation subring $O_P⊊K$ containing every rational number; $κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P$ is its residue field. For each place, $v_P(f)$ denotes the normalized integer order obtained by taking minus the integer logarithm of the maximal-ideal valuation of $O_P$; the total-function convention is $v_P(0)=0$. Write $Γ=\{0\}∪\{\operatorname{exp}(n):n∈ℤ\}$ for the multiplicative copy of the integers with zero adjoined, where $\operatorname{exp}(n)\operatorname{exp}(m)=\operatorname{exp}(n+m)$, the order on nonzero elements follows the integer exponents, and $\log\operatorname{exp}(n)=n$, $\log 0=0$. For every place $P$, every multiplicative valuation $w:K→Γ$ with $x∈O_P$ if and only if $w(x)≤1$ for all $x∈K$, and every $y∈K$ satisfying $w(y)=1$, one has $v_P(y)=0$. For $N=0$ the equation would be $1+1=1$ in characteristic zero, so no such model is supplied and assertions conditional on it are vacuous. A place $P$ means a valuation subring $O_P⊊K$ containing every rational number; $κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P$ is its residue field. Assume $h_{DVR}$: every such $O_P$ is a discrete valuation ring. Write $v_P(f)$ for minus the integer logarithm of its maximal-ideal valuation at $f$, the normalized integer order with the total-function convention $v_P(0)=0$. A separate supplied typeclass hypothesis $h_{Curve}$ also asserts that some $s∈K$ is transcendental over $ℚ$ and $K$ is finite dimensional over $ℚ(s)$; it remains a binder in this declaration even though the model supplies such data. A divisor $A$ means a finitely supported integer-valued function on all places; inequalities and addition of divisors are coefficientwise. Its degree is $\deg A=\sum_P A(P)d_P$, where $d_P=[κ(P):ℚ]$ is the finite rational vector-space dimension. Write $[P]$ for the divisor with coefficient one at $P$ and zero elsewhere. For $f∈K$, its function divisor has coefficient $\operatorname{div}(f)(P)=v_P(f)$, its zero divisor has coefficient $Z_f(P)=\max(0,v_P(f))$, and its pole divisor has coefficient $B_f(P)=\max(0,-v_P(f))$. These are the existing finitely supported divisors and all three are zero at $f=0$ by convention. For a divisor $A$, the rational vector space $L(A)$ consists exactly of $f∈K$ such that $f=0$ or $v_P(f)≥-A(P)$ at every place. Write $ℓ(A)=\operatorname{finrank}_{ℚ} L(A)$; finrank is the dimension when finite, and is the natural-number value zero for an infinite-dimensional space. For every $x∈K$ and every polynomial $p∈ℚ[X]$, $p(x)∈L(dB_x)$, where $d$ is the natural degree of $p$, taken to be zero for the zero polynomial, and $p(x)$ uses the canonical rational coefficients in $K$. No transcendence, nonzero, or positive-degree assumption is imposed. In particular the zero and constant polynomials are included.

declarations.en: Let $N$ be a natural number and let $M$ consist of an intermediate field $K$ between $ℚ$ and an algebraic closure of $ℚ(t)$, and elements $u,v∈K$, such that $u$ is transcendental over $ℚ$ (no nonzero polynomial over $ℚ$ vanishes at $u$), $u^N+v^N=1$, the subfield generated by $ℚ,u,v$ is $K$, and $K$ is finite dimensional over the subfield $ℚ(u)$ with dimension exactly $N$. There is no separate restriction on $N$; the assertion concerns supplied data satisfying all these conditions. For $N=0$ the equation would be $1+1=1$ in characteristic zero, so no such model is supplied and assertions conditional on it are vacuous. A place $P$ means a valuation subring $O_P⊊K$ containing every rational number; $κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P$ is its residue field. Assume $h_{DVR}$: every such $O_P$ is a discrete valuation ring. Write $v_P(f)$ for minus the integer logarithm of its maximal-ideal valuation at $f$, the normalized integer order with the total-function convention $v_P(0)=0$. A separate supplied typeclass hypothesis $h_{Curve}$ also asserts that some $s∈K$ is transcendental over $ℚ$ and $K$ is finite dimensional over $ℚ(s)$; it remains a binder in this declaration even though the model supplies such data. A divisor $A$ means a finitely supported integer-valued function on all places; inequalities and addition of divisors are coefficientwise. Its degree is $\deg A=\sum_P A(P)d_P$, where $d_P=[κ(P):ℚ]$ is the finite rational vector-space dimension. Write $[P]$ for the divisor with coefficient one at $P$ and zero elsewhere. For $f∈K$, its function divisor has coefficient $\operatorname{div}(f)(P)=v_P(f)$, its zero divisor has coefficient $Z_f(P)=\max(0,v_P(f))$, and its pole divisor has coefficient $B_f(P)=\max(0,-v_P(f))$. These are the existing finitely supported divisors and all three are zero at $f=0$ by convention. For every $x∈K$ transcendental over $ℚ$ (no nonzero rational polynomial vanishes at $x$) and every divisor $A$, there exist a nonzero $z∈K$ and a natural number $l$ such that $A+\operatorname{div}(z)≤lB_x$, meaning $A(P)+v_P(z)≤l\max(0,-v_P(x))$ for every place $P$. The divisor $A$ is arbitrary, including negative coefficients and the zero divisor; $l$ is allowed to be zero, and no bound or uniqueness for $l,z$ is asserted.
